finding: Every data-provider host probed returns HTTP 403 from this environment's egress proxy, with the literal response 'agent proxy: no rule or network setting allows this host'.
evidence: logs/connectivity_probe_container.json — 6 of 7 hosts at 403; control host pypi.org at 200, confirming the proxy is up and selectively allowlisted to package registries
impact: No provider bytes could be downloaded by any permitted route, in either the cloud container or on the linked computer (both probed independently).
action: Re-run reproduce_acquisition.py from an environment with outbound access to the provider hosts. No bypass was attempted and none should be.

finding: Copernicus Marine Subset/Files access requires a free registered account and the Copernicus Marine Toolbox.
evidence: Copernicus services page lists Subset, Files, Maps and a Toolbox Python API as the access methods
impact: Track A would remain HOLD on credentials even with network access, until an account exists.
action: Register free at the Copernicus Marine Service, then supply COPERNICUSMARINE_SERVICE_USERNAME and COPERNICUSMARINE_SERVICE_PASSWORD as ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES. Never in a file, never in a report.

finding: The NWS /alerts endpoint retains only SEVEN DAYS of alerts. The provider directs users to NCEI for an official CAP archive.
evidence: NWS API documentation page, quoted: alerts cover 'the past seven days'; also 'only 7 days of observations are retained for weather stations'
impact: This is the most consequential finding of Pass 3A and it is NOT an artefact of the sandbox. The primary Track B candidate cannot supply 2020-2024 issued records at any time, from any network.
action: Redirect Track B to the NCEI NDFD archive (see P3A-04). Do not treat a current alert as historical.

finding: NCEI NDFD states periods of record that DO cover the study window: NDFD by WMO header from 2004-06-06 to present, and an AWS Open Data mirror from 2020-04-16 to present.
impact: This is the concrete Track B route. The AWS mirror window 2020-04-16 onward overlaps the 2020-2024 replay window for all but the first 3.5 months.
action: Attempt the AWS Open Data NDFD mirror (registry.opendata.aws/noaa-ndfd) and the NCEI THREDDS endpoint. Note AIRS requests for pre-2008 data are limited to one day each, and NCEI warns of delayed archival during a cloud migration.

finding: The Copernicus pages retrieved list variable NAMES but state neither standard_name nor UNITS.
evidence: 03_environmental_metadata.csv — standard_name and units are 'NOT STATED on the pages retrieved' for all 18 variables
impact: Track A step 4 (record variable standard/long name and units, flag incompatible definitions) cannot be completed from page text. It requires the NetCDF attributes.
action: Read units from the NetCDF variable attributes once a file is obtained. Do not assume them.

finding: The product offers several distinct wave-height and wave-period definitions, including primary swell, secondary swell, wind-wave and total significant height, plus three different mean-period definitions from spectral moments.
impact: A18.1 used a single 'wave_height (m)' and 'wave_period (s)' pair from Open-Meteo. Those are NOT automatically the same quantities as any of these. Silently substituting one for another would be a definition error, which Track C forbids.
action: When a file is obtained, map each A18.1 variable to a specific Copernicus variable by standard_name and units, and record any definition that does not correspond.

finding: None of the six mandatory Google Doc references could be opened in this environment.
evidence: docs.google.com is not reachable through the egress proxy; no document connector is attached to this session
impact: The geographic-scope amendment, Pass 3 shortlist, Pass 1 plan, A18.3 endpoint readiness, Pass 4 provenance rules and A18.2-R findings were NOT reviewed from source. I worked from the task's own explicit requirements plus the LOCAL A18.1-A18.2-R artefacts, which are in this repository.
action: Supply these as pasted text or local files if any requirement in them differs from the task text. I have NOT asserted that they were reviewed.

finding: The project already holds hash-verified environmental CSVs from A18.1. Re-labelling them as a Pass 3A acquisition would satisfy the quality gates on paper while acquiring nothing.
impact: Explicitly NOT done. Those files are Open-Meteo-derived, acquired in an earlier pass, and are neither a Copernicus subset nor an issued source.
action: Keep the distinction. Pass 3A acquired zero new bytes and says so.

finding: Provider metadata was obtained through a document fetcher that returns processed page text, not raw bytes.
evidence: 01 and 03 registers are tiered DOCUMENTED_ONLY throughout
impact: That output cannot be byte-hashed and is not a provider file. It is sufficient for recording what the provider STATES and insufficient for any gate requiring a parsed data file.
action: Treat every DOCUMENTED_ONLY value as provisional until read from a NetCDF or CAP file.

finding: No region was selected and no bounding box or UTC range was fixed for Track A.
evidence: Track A step 2 requires a subset choice; with no download path the choice would be untestable
impact: reproduce_acquisition.py therefore ships a DEFAULT bounded box and range as parameters, clearly marked as a proposal that has never been executed against the provider.
action: Confirm or change the default before the first real run.

finding: The report-vs-artifact audit (gate A3A-07) required SEVEN corrections to its own guards before it ran clean. Three guards were substantively wrong: one flagged negated disclaimers as affirmative safety claims, one flagged documented credential VARIABLE NAMES as leaked secrets, and one self-matched because the audit script contains its own search patterns. The other four were the same defect repeated: a hand-typed prose string that did not match the document (markdown emphasis markers, a line-wrapped sentence, and 'could not be opened' where both register and report read 'None ... could be opened').
evidence: logs/report_audit.json; the corrected guards and their history are commented in audit_report_against_artifacts.py
impact: No artifact was wrong: every failure was in the checker, and the fix was always to the guard, never to the report. But it is the SAME failure mode recorded in A18.2-R — hand-written prose drifting from computed artifacts — now appearing in the tool built to catch it. A guard that cries wolf erodes trust in the gate as surely as one that stays silent.
action: G-15 was ultimately rewritten to check STRUCTURED DATA (does register row P3A-07 exist, does the report cite that ID) instead of matching prose. That is the pattern the A18.2-R remediation spec called for and it is the one that should be used for all future report checks: bind to artefact fields and IDs, never to typed sentences.
